The contrast between contempt for the person and an argument about how insight is shown is accurate.

The two verses do not speak of the same thing. Acharakkovai concerns one who scorns (இகழ்வான்) பார்ப்பார் among the elements, the cow, sun and moon, while Kural 134 concerns the பார்ப்பான்'s own birth lost when பிறப்பொழுக்கம் குன்ற. That reverence from others lapses is an inference, and 'disagree' claims a tension the link's type does not make. The note does not endorse the rule.

எல்லில் பிறன்கடை நின்றொழுகுவான் points to the act verse 9 names as உரிமையில் பெண்டிரைக் காமுற்று வாழ்தல். One verse makes it a fool's காதல், the other sets it among acts of those who தூங்குபவர், between the elephant and the snake. The pair shows the book judging the same act by desire and by danger.

Both verses use the ox pulling a salt cart out of the mire, a distinctive image of the coastal trade road: ஆரைச் சாகாட்டு ஆழ்ச்சி போக்கும் உரனுடை நோன்பகடு against அள்ளல் அழுந்திய சாகாட்டு ... வாங்கும் தந்தை கைபூண் பகடு. Strength in praise and strain in love (வருந்தி வெய்ய உயிர்க்கும்) is an accurate contrast, though in 140 the ox is also pulling, not crushed under the cart.

The Siddhar's argument denies the consistency of the rule the Acharakkovai states, and the note treats the rule as the text's norm.

ஒப்ப நாடி அத்தக ஒறுத்தி matches தக்காங்கு நாடி ... ஒத்தாங்கு ஒறுப்பது: the same act named in the same terms of inquiry and proportion, a specific meeting. Line 5's softened sentence (அடி பொருந்தி ... தண்டமும் தணிதி) is a real addition that 561 lacks. 'Drawn out of praise' is hedged as 'reads like'.

The link equates the Kural's ஒழுக்கம் with Acharakkovai's ஆசாரம். The verse makes the eight virtues the வித்து of ஆசாரம், but it does not say the conduct 'is not a set of rules', since the book itself goes on to give rules. The teaches therefore overstates, and the pair otherwise rests on the shared praise of conduct.

The two do meet on keeping learning unspoken before those unfit for it. The quatrain implies waste, not Pazhamozhi's turning of நல்லவும் into தீயவாம், so the list_adds is untrue.

The note names the reading the conflict depends on: புலை as a birth-group person, set beside நாய் and the heavenly bodies as a barred sight. On that reading the rule ranks by birth, which பிறப்பொக்கும் எல்லா உயிர்க்கும் denies. The note states the rule as the text's norm without endorsing it.

பெருமையுடையார் இனத்தின் அகறல் is the act Kural 450 ranks as worse than many enemies (நல்லார் தொடர்கை விடல்). Thirikadugam's predicate முழுமக்கள் காதல் supplies the motive, so the pair shows a harm that is wanted, which neither verse shows alone.
